LESSON: READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we read? 2. How can we read faster?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text of about 300 words for comprehension,
2. apply appropriate reading skills to obtain both factual and inferential information from a text,
3. recommend intensive reading in their day-to- day life. SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension.
2. Explain Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: read a variety of print and non-print texts of about 300 words,
4. Show that you can: read a text of about 300 words for comprehension,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why do we read? 2. How can we read faster?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a variety of print and non-print texts of about 300 words,
2. Skim through a digital text of about 300 words focusing mainly on the title and illustrations,
